bug_semantics: Outbound HTTP/1.1 start-line fields are serialized to the wire without neutralizing CR/LF or other illegal bytes. HTTPRequestEncoder writes HTTPRequestHead.uri and HTTPMethod.RAW verbatim into the request line; HTTPResponseEncoder writes a custom HTTPResponseStatus.reasonPhrase verbatim into the status line. An attacker who can influence those fields (proxy-forwarded URL/method, client redirect to a crafted URL, or a custom reason phrase) injects a second request or response on the same connection (request smuggling / response splitting, CWE-93). From 2.42.0 the default NIOHTTPRequestHeadersValidator / NIOHTTPResponseHeadersValidator (enableOutboundHeaderValidation=true on addHTTPClientHandlers / addHTTPServerHandlers) only gated header names and values via areValidToSend, so a CRLF URI/method/reason still reached the encoder.
flaw_origin: The request-line injection sink was first written in 976f4752dfffe5b07e53562226a3e180f82a95d6 (2017-11-02), which added HTTPRequestEncoder writing buffer.write(string: request.uri) and HTTPMethod.write for .RAW(value) with no character-set check. Immediate parent c18db56fc29dc0aabe6e7503798056eaf3365a6d already had HTTPRequest.uri / HTTPMethod.RAW types and HTTPResponseStatus.write of reasonPhrase, but had no HTTPRequestEncoder and no HTTPMethod.write.
